calls.reason: The only measurement is the Scientific Reports citation study, with outputs from April 2023. It shows heavy fabrication on one specialized task, which is too thin and too early to show how common falsehoods were in ordinary use around October 2023.

The full Bing answer was never recovered, so the falsehoods can't be counted. The Congressional Record confirms the Speaker's office was vacant, and NBC's report undercuts one of Marcus's points (that Cheney was ineligible). Neither settles the count of seven.

The evidence is mixed. In the Hoes study, ChatGPT sorted both true and false claims well above chance, but on the FELM benchmark most ChatGPT detectors showed no fact-checking ability. The wording is also rhetorical and has no threshold.

This is a causal claim, and no controlled evidence isolates the cause. The GPT-4 report confirms next-token pretraining, and Google's Bard double-check feature shows some deployed checking against the web, but neither settles the claim.
